title: SLO integration roadmap and change ladder
content:
Purpose: capture a pragmatic, cross-team plan to integrate service-level objectives into product delivery cycles across platform, runtime, and feature teams, with a lightweight change ladder to reduce blast radius for SLO changes.

Audience: SRE leads, product engineering managers, platform owners, QA, solutions engineers. Use this as the canonical working note for the next 8 weeks.

Summary (one line): phased SLO onboarding + change-ladder that lets teams iterate on SLO targets and alerts with controlled exposure, automated guardrails, and rollback plans.

Why this approach?
- Observed problem: teams flip alerts or tweak targets ad hoc; causes noisy paging and config churn.
- Goal: reduce noise, shorten time-to-safe-SLO, and ensure predictable coordination when targets change.

High-level phases (8 weeks):
1) Discovery & alignment (wk1-2)
   - Quick inventory: every service owning a customer-facing route -> list of current SLOs, alerts, burn-rate thresholds. (owner: feature leads)
   - Stakeholder alignment session: SRE, product, runtime, QA. Agenda: existing pain, acceptable error budget policy, rollout constraints.
   - Deliverable: "SLO inventory + ownership map" (spreadsheet).

2) Standardization & templates (wk3)
   - Provide SLO template: objective, measurement window, calculation query, alert thresholds (warning/critical), burn-rate remediation steps.
   - Platform infra: ensure Prometheus/Telemetry queries standardized and documented. (owner: platform eng)
   - Deliverable: SLO template + example filled for 3 pilot services.

3) Pilot + change ladder trial (wk4-6)
   - Pick 3 pilot services across product and infra surface area (low-risk, medium-risk, high-risk).
   - Apply change ladder for any SLO change: "Observation -> Alerting milestone -> Canary target -> Full target".
   - Canary rules: 48h canary at 5% traffic or low-traffic window; auto-revert on exceed burn-rate.
   - Runbook stub: step-by-step rollback and postmortem triggers.

4) Scale & bake into delivery cadence (wk7-8)
   - Add SLO gates into PR checklist for routes with >X qps.
   - Integrate with release calendar and automated tests that simulate load to validate SLOs (owner: release eng + QA).
   - Deliverable: SLO PR checklist + CI smoke tests.

Change ladder (detailed):
- Level 0: Observation (no alert change)
  - Notes: Record intent in the SLO issue, add to backlog. No automated action.
- Level 1: Soft alert (warning only)
  - Fire a non-paging channel alert; monitor for 7 days. Document observed differences.
- Level 2: Canary target
  - Apply new target to a canary slice (traffic/routing or reduced threshold). Run 48h and collect metrics.
- Level 3: Gradual rollout
  - 25% -> 50% -> 100% over pre-defined windows, with automated checks at each step.
- Level 4: Full switch and verification
  - Update runbooks, escalation targets, and dashboards. Schedule a post-adoption review after 30 days.

Operational guardrails (must-have):
- Every SLO change requires an associated ticket with: rationale, expected customer impact, rollback plan, and stakeholders.
- Automated safety net: new SLOs trigger a burn-rate policy that halts rollout if burn-rate > X for 1h.
- Instrumentation: must have at least one synthetic probe and one real-user metric for any customer-facing SLO.

Onboarding checklist for feature teams (short):
- Create SLO ticket from template.
- Attach queries and dashboard links.
- Assign an SRE reviewer.
- Run canary tests in staging with the CI workload generator.
- Schedule canary window in calendar and notify on-call.

Roles & responsibilities (quick mapping):
- Feature team PM/Eng: define the customer-level objective and acceptance criteria.
- SRE: review SLO math, define alerts, own rollback.
- Platform: make sure metrics emitters and runtime configs support canary flags.
- QA/Perf: run the synthetic/load checks in the CI pipeline.
- Solutions Eng: notify customers for externally visible SLO changes.

Success metrics (to measure experiment):
- Reduction in paging due to SLO changes (target: -30% in 3 months).
- Median time to safe SLO adoption (target: < 10 days from ticket open to full adoption).
- % of services using SLO template (target: 75% of routes > threshold qps).

Risks & open questions (callouts):
- Risk: teams may treat soft alerts as "done" and skip canary. Mitigation: require SRE signoff for Level 2 moves.
- Q: how to handle dependent services? Proposed: dependency matrix and coordinated canary windows.
- Q: thresholds for different tiers (free vs enterprise customers). Need product input.

Short-term action items (this week):
- Priya: draft SLO template and share in #sre-reliability (due: 2026-04-14).
- Liam: extract initial SLO inventory from telemetry (due: 2026-04-16).
- Maria: schedule stakeholder alignment slot (30–60m) and build agenda (due: 2026-04-15).
- Omar: prototype a CI canary job that can flip targets via feature-flag (due: 2026-04-20).

Longer tasks (who/when):
- Platform eng: add API for canary routing flags (owner: Platform infra, target: 2026-06-01).
- Release eng: add SLO gate to release checklist for major releases (target: 2026-07-01).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a lightweight "SLO health" badge in PRs.
- Tie cost/latency tradeoff into Optimize recommendations so product can choose cheaper quantized model with known SLO delta.
- Maybe automate a weekly digest of services approaching burn rates.

Appendix: example SLO ticket template (paste):
- Title: SLO: route x.y.z target 99.5% p99 latency (30d)
- Owner: team / pm / oncall
- Measurement: query (promQL) + dashboard link
- Alerts: warning (2% error budget/7d), critical (5% error budget/24h)
- Canary plan: dates, traffic slice, rollback plan
- Dependencies: list service IDs
- Rollout schedule: day-by-day plan

Unresolved: exact burn-rate thresholds and whether burn-rate automation blocks or flags. Put on agenda for stakeholder session.
